subject: Maths
title: Non-linear simultaneous equations
subtitle: Simultaneous Equations · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can solve simultaneous equations where one equation is linear and one is quadratic.

key_vocab.definition: Non-linear simultaneous equations involve one linear equation and one equation with a squared term (e.g. circle or quadratic). Use substitution to solve.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can solve simultaneous equations where one equation is linear and one is quadratic.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Non-linear simultaneous equations -- Non-linear simultaneous equations involve one linear equation and one equation with a squared term (e.g. circle or quadratic). Use substitution to solve.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Substitute the linear equation into the quadratic to get a single equation in one variable. Then solve the resulting quadratic.
y = x + 1; x² + y² = 5 ⇒ x² + (x+1)² = 5
Replace y with the linear expression, then solve

Key examples:
  ✓ y = x + 1 and x² + y² = 5: substitute y  (circle and line)
  ✓ y = 2x and y = x² − 3: set equal  (parabola and line)
  ✓ Usually gives two pairs of solutions  (line crosses curve twice)
  ✗ Use elimination for non-linear equations  (must use substitution)
  ✗ Non-linear systems always have exactly 2 solutions  (can have 0, 1, or 2)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – line and circle
  Solve y = x + 1 and x² + y² = 5
  Substitute: x² + (x+1)² = 5 ⇒ x² + x² + 2x + 1 = 5
  2x² + 2x − 4 = 0 ⇒ x² + x − 2 = 0 ⇒ (x+2)(x−1) = 0
  x = −2, y = −1 or x = 1, y = 2
  (−2, −1) and (1, 2)
  (Find x values from the quadratic, then substitute back for y.)

Example 2 – line and parabola
  Solve y = 2x + 1 and y = x² − 2
  Set equal: x² − 2 = 2x + 1
  x² − 2x − 3 = 0 ⇒ (x−3)(x+1) = 0
  x = 3, y = 7 or x = −1, y = −1
  (3, 7) and (−1, −1)
  (When both equations equal y, set the right-hand sides equal.)

sections.title: Line and parabola
sections.content:
Solve each pair simultaneously.

(a) y = x + 2 and y = x²
(b) y = 3x and y = x² + 2
(c) y = x + 6 and y = x²
(d) y = 2x + 3 and y = x² + x + 1

sections.title: Line and circle
sections.content:
Solve each pair simultaneously.

(a) y = x and x² + y² = 8
(b) y = x + 2 and x² + y² = 10
(c) x + y = 5 and x² + y² = 13
(d) y = 2x and x² + y² = 20

sections.title: Product relationships
sections.content:
Solve these pairs.

(a) x + y = 7 and xy = 12
(b) x + y = 10 and xy = 21
(c) x − y = 2 and xy = 15
(d) x + y = 9 and xy = 20

sections.title: Harder problems
sections.content:
Solve each pair simultaneously.

(a) y = 2x − 1 and y = x² − 3x + 3
(b) x + 2y = 7 and x² + y² = 10
(c) y = x + 1 and x² + 2y² = 6
(d) 2x + y = 5 and x² + y² = 5

sections.title: Mixed non-linear
sections.content:
Solve each system.

(a) y = x − 1 and x² + y² = 25
(b) y = 3 − x and y = x² − x − 1
(c) x + y = 4 and x² + 3y = 10
(d) y = x + 3 and 2x² + y² = 27
(e) y = 2x and x² − y = 3

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ To solve non-linear simultaneous equations, use substitution
✗ You can use elimination for quadratic simultaneous equations
✓ A line and a circle can intersect at 0, 1, or 2 points
✗ Non-linear systems always have exactly 2 solutions
✓ After substitution, you solve the resulting quadratic equation
